A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from Actra to Astra. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions and relocation of material.

before.justification: V1 reports original robot-learning evaluations on ManiSkill, Franka Kitchen and Push-T, including quantitative comparisons, component ablations and qualitative execution examples.

after.justification: V2 reports original VIMA-Bench and CALVIN evaluations and retains the ManiSkill, Franka Kitchen and Push-T results, alongside ablations and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: Trajectory attention and parallel action queries are retained. However, Section 3.3 substantially revises contrastive learning: positives gain image augmentation, the separate prompt/state/action negative families become mixed state/action negatives incorporating augmented samples, and trajectory encoding gains a linear layer after pooling. These are procedural changes beyond renaming the objective CDL.

E1.justification: V2 adds VIMA-Bench, including multimodal instructions and novel meta-tasks, and CALVIN, including generalization to an unseen environment. ManiSkill remains, while Franka Kitchen and Push-T move to Appendix A.10. Thus coverage expands from three environments to five rather than replacing the two relocated benchmarks.

E2.justification: New reported comparisons include DT, Flamingo and object-token Gato on VIMA-Bench, and MCIL, OpenVLA, MDT, RoboFlamingo and GR-1 on CALVIN. Appendix A.9 also reports an unsuccessful π0 evaluation without numerical results. The existing ManiSkill and Franka Kitchen/Push-T comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: V2 introduces substantial new protocols: VIMA-Bench's four generalization levels and 10-epoch training, and CALVIN's ABC-to-D evaluation using the language-annotated 1% subset, five-task sequences and 20-epoch training. It adds a 38M configuration. ManiSkill's reported Gato and VIMA sizes change from 309M/695M to 198M/525M; this does not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 extends component ablations to VIMA-Bench, adds training loss/accuracy curves and with/without-CDL execution examples, but removes the separate vision-, language- and action-negative ablations. The attention heatmaps are retained in Appendix A.3, and the regrasp example remains the same underlying case.

E5.justification: V2 newly specifies 100 evaluation trials per VIMA-Bench task. The existing 50-trial ManiSkill, 50-run Franka Kitchen and 30-trial Push-T counts remain. Neither version specifies independent training-seed replication, confidence intervals or significance tests; the added trial count does not establish increased replication of retained experiments.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive VIMA-Bench and CALVIN results, including Astra's 97.08% VIMA-Bench L1 success and 3.29 CALVIN average sequence length. Retained benchmark comparison scores largely match v1. However, ManiSkill's 'w/o Both' ablation changes from 83.3/79.4/68.0 to 72.33/76.00/67.00 for easy/medium/hard tasks. Separate negative-type results and several aggregate results are removed.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 revises the formal construction of negative trajectories from three modality-specific families to mixed state/action negatives, changing the negative set used in the contrastive objective. The standard InfoNCE form, attention-mask mathematics, connection-count expression and diffusion-loss formulas remain. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: A central contribution is redefined: v1 emphasizes explicit alignment of vision, language and action, while v2 claims that CDL learns environment dynamics and provides a lightweight alternative to generative dynamics learning. This claim appears throughout the abstract, introduction and conclusion. The trajectory-attention/action-query contribution remains.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations for negative-sample difficulty and CDL's reduced VIMA-Bench L4 performance, while dropping v1's explicit component-synergy interpretation. It replaces the earlier computational and multi-embodiment limitations with discussion of simulation-based evaluation and possible 3D inputs. Appendix A.4 newly explains that direct integration into autoregressive large VLAs requires substantial retraining.

D1.justification: V2 adds a repository link, benchmark-specific encoders, action representations, training budgets and hyperparameters, including the 38M configuration and five ManiSkill training epochs. Conversely, it omits v1's segment/timestep positional-embedding specification, frozen-T5 statement and explicit contrastive warmup schedule. These omissions do not establish corresponding implementation changes.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially repositioned around a distinction between large and generalized VLAs and between generative and contrastive dynamics learning. New discussions include OpenVLA, π0, GR-2 and world-model research such as Dreamer. This goes beyond the change from numbered to author-year citations.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work and contrastive-learning narrative, renames Actra to Astra, and changes the title and author list. It reorganizes the experimental sections and appendices, moves two benchmarks out of the main text, and adds a notation glossary and several explanatory subsections.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Architecture and contrastive-learning diagrams are redesigned; attention comparisons, training curves and execution panels are added. Attention heatmaps move to the appendix, the generalization bar chart disappears, and the combined Franka Kitchen/Push-T table becomes two appendix tables.

improvement.justification: V1's generalization evidence chiefly concerns held-out object attributes in ManiSkill. V2 directly tests multimodal instructions, novel meta-tasks and transfer to an unseen CALVIN environment, with additional component ablations and stronger comparison sets. This substantially strengthens support for the architecture's applicability and exposes a CDL generalization limitation. Omitted implementation details and unexplained ManiSkill parameter-count revisions weaken reproducibility, but the expanded, targeted validation provides a substantial net improvement.
